strengths: Makes an important conceptual contribution distinguishing unfaithfulness from incompleteness in CoT evaluation
Comprehensive multi-method empirical evaluation using Filler Tokens, FUR, faithful@k, Logit Lens, and causal mediation analysis
Novel faithful@k metric cleverly adapts sampling-based evaluation to address greedy decoding assumptions
Thorough experimental documentation across 3 models, 3 datasets, and 3 hint types with detailed hyperparameter reporting
Well-motivated critique of Biasing Features metric that conflates orthogonal concepts
Honest discussion of computational limitations and methodological limitations (LLM-judge reliability, sample sizes)
weaknesses: Limited to small models (3-8B parameters) with no evaluation on larger reasoning models despite those being the focus of recent unfaithfulness claims
Inconsistent results across alternative metrics raise questions about why they disagree so substantially (Filler Tokens 20-40%, FUR 50%+, but varies widely)
Puzzling divergence in faithful@k results: Professor hint shows strong improvement with k while Metadata/Black Squares plateau, suggesting mechanisms more complex than token budget incompleteness
Small effect sizes in causal mediation analysis (many estimates 1e-6 to 1e-7) with unclear practical significance despite statistical significance
LLM-as-judge achieves only 31% recall/precision for positive cases, missing many actual hint verbalizations and potentially weakening claims
Critical sample size issues in several conditions (Llama-3-8B with Black Squares: n=3-5 instances) undermining statistical reliability
Post-hoc rationalization analysis underdeveloped: direct effects often exceed indirect effects and late-layer hint emergence could support post-hoc claims rather than refute them
Results highly heterogeneous across models (Gemma reaches 0.9 faithful@k under Professor but 0 under Metadata; Llama-3-8B consistently lower) without explanation for why
Dataset scope limited to multiple-choice reasoning tasks; generalization to open-ended generation or other domains unclear
Artificial hint setup (random injected cues) limits insights into whether models actually rely on decision-relevant factors in real use

strengths: Addresses an important narrative in the field by systematically questioning the Biasing Features metric's equation of non-verbalization with unfaithfulness
Proposes a conceptually useful distinction between incompleteness and unfaithfulness that advances how we think about CoT evaluation
Employs a comprehensive multi-method approach (alternative metrics, faithful@k, causal mediation, Logit Lens) rather than relying on a single evaluation framework
Well-executed experimental work within its scope, with careful controls across three datasets, three models, and three hint injection methods
Thorough experimental documentation and reproducibility commitment (code release, detailed appendices with hyperparameters and implementation details)
Clear presentation with effective figures and generally well-written throughout
weaknesses: Severely limited model scope—only tests small models (3B-8B parameters), while field focuses on much larger models and reasoning models that may exhibit different CoT behaviors; acknowledged computational constraints but critically limits generalizability

Narrow task scope restricted to multiple-choice QA with synthetic hints, leaving open questions about whether findings generalize to code generation, mathematical reasoning, complex planning, or other domains

Alternative metrics (Filler Tokens, FUR, Logit Lens) do not directly measure faithfulness; the paper sidesteps the fundamental question of defining what faithfulness should mean and merely substitutes different metrics without establishing their validity

Causal Mediation Analysis overinterpreted: (1) assumes clean separation between direct/indirect effects in entangled LLM systems, (2) NIE>0 only proves CoT affects output, not that it reflects actual reasoning, (3) post-hoc rationalizations can still causally mediate predictions, (4) effect sizes often tiny (1e-6), raising questions about significance

Faithful@k metric conflates sampling diversity with faithfulness; the measure is almost tautological (more samples → eventually hit different outputs) and doesn't clearly distinguish incompleteness from unfaithfulness
LLM-as-judge validation is weak with only 80% agreement and concerning precision/recall (31%/36%) for the core hint verbalization detection task; high false-negative rate could weaken main claims

Empty/degenerate CoT problem incompletely addressed—Llama-3-8B-Instruct generates many empty CoTs especially affecting Filler Tokens/FUR evaluations; excluding these rather than investigating may bias results

Central claim that 'much apparent unfaithfulness is incompleteness' is overstated: incompleteness is never formally defined, alternative explanations for each piece of evidence exist, and the paper doesn't adequately consider that both unfaithfulness and incompleteness could coexist
No direct comparison with original Biasing Features papers using their own evaluation protocols; tests on familiar datasets rather than establishing that conclusions contradict prior claims

Logit Lens analysis is suggestive but weak—hints appearing in top-5 logits doesn't prove they drive reasoning; pattern identification is hand-wavy and doesn't account for distributed computation across many tokens

strengths: Important and timely critique of influential recent claims about CoT unfaithfulness using rigorous methodology
Comprehensive multi-method approach with three complementary lines of evidence (metric comparison, faithful@k, causal mediation analysis) rather than relying on single metric
Extensive experimental coverage across three models, three datasets, and three hint types with proper statistical treatment (bootstrapped confidence intervals)
Novel faithful@k metric elegantly adapted from pass@k to test incompleteness vs. genuine unfaithfulness hypothesis
Conceptually important distinction between faithfulness and incompleteness that challenges the assumptions underlying prior work
Excellent presentation with clear organization, informative figures, and well-articulated arguments
Strong reproducibility support with detailed methods, implementation details in appendices, and promised code release
weaknesses: Limited to small models (3-8B parameters) while recent high-profile unfaithfulness claims focus on large reasoning models; generalization to larger models remains unclear

Inconsistent improvements from increased inference budget: faithful@k reaches ~90% for Professor hint but shows minimal improvement for Metadata/Black Squares hints, undermining the incompleteness explanation for 2/3 of conditions
LLM-as-judge for hint verbalization detection achieves only 80% accuracy with very low precision (36%) and recall (31%), introducing potential systematic bias in all verbalization judgments
Restricted domain scope: all experiments use multiple-choice QA; no evaluation on open-ended tasks or real-world applications limiting claims about CoT faithfulness broadly

Causal Mediation Analysis results are indirect and difficult to interpret: non-zero indirect effects are expected, relative magnitudes of NDE vs NIE vary erratically without clear guidance on concerning effect sizes
Missing analysis of genuine failure modes: paper doesn't characterize when CoTs are unfaithful across all metrics, limiting understanding of actual problem cases
FUR evaluation restricted to instances where no-CoT and CoT predictions match, often excluding empty/degenerate CoTs, potentially biasing the sample

strengths: Addresses an important and timely debate about CoT faithfulness with comprehensive experimental validation across multiple metrics, models (3B-70B), and datasets

Introduces novel diagnostic metric (faithful@k) that can distinguish incompleteness from unfaithfulness through differential behavior across hint types, and novel application of Causal Mediation Analysis
Comprehensive empirical coverage with multiple complementary faithfulness metrics (Biasing Features, Filler Tokens, FUR) and extensive robustness checks addressing methodological concerns
Clear, measured framing that avoids overclaiming—argues that absence of hint verbalization doesn't prove unfaithfulness rather than claiming all CoTs are faithful
Shows non-trivial fraction (50%+) of Biasing Features-flagged unfaithful CoTs are classified as faithful by alternative metrics across models and datasets
weaknesses: LLM-as-judge achieves only 36% precision and 31% recall, substantially undermining confidence in the ~80% unfaithfulness rates in Figure 2 that motivate the paper, even though false negatives are partially addressed

Causal Mediation Analysis effect sizes are often very small (e-6 to e-11 scale) with unclear practical significance; NIE and NDE sometimes have overlapping confidence intervals, making interpretation difficult

Faithful@k cannot distinguish incompleteness from non-exhaustiveness (acknowledged by authors); the explanation for differential behavior across hint types (sycophancy) is speculative and not definitively validated

Qualitative examples in Table 6 show CoTs with factually incorrect reasoning and problematic semantic reinterpretations (e.g., 'electrical path' → 'open'), which undermine rather than support main thesis; only 4 examples provided
Limited scope to artificial constrained setting (multi-hop QA with 2-4 multiple choice answers); generalization to open-ended reasoning, code generation, or long-form tasks unclear
Somewhat incremental contribution as recent work (Barez et al., Korbak et al.) already advocates for broader evaluation approaches and acknowledges communication utility of CoTs
Lacks human evaluation of CoT quality, analysis of correlation with downstream task performance, and practical guidance for practitioners on how to use findings

strengths: Addresses an important and influential narrative in recent CoT faithfulness literature; contributes useful scrutiny of broad claims
Comprehensive multi-method experimental design (Filler Tokens, FUR, faithful@k, Logit Lens, Causal Mediation Analysis) with scope across multiple models (3.2B-70B) and datasets
Well-motivated conceptual distinction between unfaithfulness and incompleteness that advances the conversation beyond binary faithful/unfaithful classifications
Thoughtful faithful@k metric that provides indirect evidence for the incompleteness hypothesis by testing whether more inference budget increases hint verbalization
Causal Mediation Analysis introduces a novel approach to test whether non-verbalized hints causally influence predictions, moving beyond correlation
Honest treatment of limitations (LLM-as-judge performance, faithful@k interpretation issues, incompleteness vs. exhaustiveness distinction); supports reproducibility
weaknesses: LLM-as-judge with 31% recall and 36% precision fundamentally undermines the core evaluation—false negatives mean some CoTs classified as unfaithful by Biasing Features may actually be faithful, weakening the main claims; gpt-4o comparison (80% precision) relegated to appendix

faithful@k plateaus under Black Squares and Metadata hints, directly contradicting the incompleteness hypothesis; post-hoc explanation about hint-type-dependent processing is speculative and underdeveloped

Causal Mediation Analysis effects are small in magnitude (1e-5 to 1e-8) and show wide confidence intervals; causally mediating some of a hint's effect does not prove CoT faithfulness or that the reasoning explanation reflects actual computation

Qualitative examples (Table 6) show CoTs inventing false reasoning steps (e.g., misinterpreting 'electrical path'), which appears to be unfaithfulness rather than incompleteness, contradicting the paper's framing
Model-dependent results complicate generalization: Llama-3-8B produces degenerate CoTs, Qwen-3-32B shows opposite patterns (negative NIE), yet these discrepancies are not adequately explained

May strawman or mischaracterize prior work: authors like Barez and Korbak don't claim absolute unfaithfulness but rather test whether CoTs mention known decision factors—the disagreement may reflect complementary measures rather than Biasing Features being wrong
Experimental setup inconsistency: greedy decoding for Biasing Features but sampling for faithful@k; limited datasets (three QA tasks); artificial hint injection method
Cannot distinguish incompleteness from non-exhaustiveness, limiting the strength of conclusions about why hints aren't verbalized

strengths: Comprehensive multi-metric evaluation addressing an important debate in CoT faithfulness research; the reframing of unfaithfulness vs. incompleteness is conceptually valuable
Excellent experimental rigor with multiple datasets, models, hint types, and generalization to larger models; detailed reproducibility materials and promised code release
Well-executed complementary methodology (Filler Tokens, FUR, faithful@k, Logit Lens, Causal Mediation Analysis) provides triangulation and strengthens confidence in findings
Novel practical implications: cautions against optimizing for hint verbalization, with important consequences for future interpretability-focused training pipelines
Clear presentation with effective visualizations and comprehensive appendices; logical flow and well-articulated conceptual arguments
weaknesses: LLM-as-judge has low precision (36%) and recall (31%), with concerning 31% false negative rate; while robustness checks help, this limitation directly affects core Biasing Features claims

faithful@k cannot distinguish at instance level between two interpretations: (1) hint-shaped reasoning but incomplete verbalization vs. (2) occasional faithfulness with cherry-picked runs; aggregate patterns help but leave individual cases ambiguous

Causal Mediation Analysis effects sometimes extremely small (10^-6 to 10^-8) with confidence intervals overlapping zero; interpretation of negative NIE values as 'suppressive role' underdeveloped; practical significance unclear
Limited case-by-case analysis of metric disagreements; qualitative examples feel anecdotal; insufficient investigation of when Biasing Features genuinely fails vs. simply incomplete

Artificial experimental setup with random hint injection may not reflect real-world reasoning failures; task domain limited to multi-hop reasoning; generalization to other reasoning types unclear; datasets conceptually similar
